ratings_why.fun: The shelf-life timing puzzle is a good one, but the board never keeps its growth, so every cycle has a dark fight that costs Health and a late carry has to come from another tribe.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7: buffs that expire on a Moon the opponent can see make every buy a question of when, and the only way to keep stats is to hand them to other tribes; no tribe today plays like that.

verdict_why: Two cards need clearer or capped text (Charm-Pedlar's repeat trigger, Leveret's target) and the core timing explanation is off by one turn.

points.text: Charm-Pedlar pays on every New Moon, so several Pedlars with Dew-Pond Scryers, Moon-Caller and The Hare in the Moon can run a whole cycle in one turn for more gold than it costs. Add "Once a turn".
Leveret in the Form's "first unit in front of it" can't be read: a back-row Leveret has two diagonal units in front and a front-row one has none. Say which one, or let it pick in reading order.

The play text says a buff on the Waxing turn lasts four fights, but by the cycle as written a New Moon-turn buff lasts four and a Waxing one three. Fix the explanation so the core timing is taught right.
Only Dusk-Runner (Tier 5) covers the dark New Moon fight, and the first wipe lands on turn 4 just as hero damage starts. A Tier 2 or 3 Hare that is strongest on the New Moon would smooth the climb.
Sister Silverpenny is dead in a pure Hare board. Let her fall back to copying your biggest Hare's text when you have no unit that isn't a Hare.

standouts.why: Chalk-Cutter doubles light by seating, so where you put it is a real decision every Full Moon.
Old Wat is the tribe's loophole in one card: a jack beside lit Hares who keeps half their light for good.
Giddy Jill's rising X teaches the cycle and rewards buying it early in the phase.

weakest.why: Sister Silverpenny depends entirely on other tribes and is hard to read or price.
Spring-Ring Jill is a plain stat body whose only twist is being worse on one turn.
Charm-Pedlar does almost nothing before turn 8, then loops in the Fast Moon.

flags.note: Multiple Charm-Pedlars plus Wax effects can turn repeated New Moons into net gold in one turn.
Mother Meikle Care and Old Wat bank a share of each cycle permanently; with a fast Moon the Moon-Scour's counter climbs, so the banked amount grows each cycle rather than staying linear.
Golden Dame Waxwell with golden Chalk-Cutters and the Moon-Scour gives one-fight spikes in the thousands; capped by the reset, but worth the owner's eye.
Which unit counts as "the first unit in front of it" isn't defined.
